html:
The Karasuk culture was a group of late Bronze Age societies of southern Siberia and the eastern steppe, from about 1500 to 800 BCE. Its sites range from the Aral Sea to the upper Yenisei River, and south to the Altai and the Tian Shan. Its heart was the Minusinsk Basin, where the earlier Afanasevo culture had also lived.

Karasuk people were herders of cattle and sheep who also farmed a little. They followed the Andronovo cultures in the region. Their bronze knives, with curved blades and handles topped by animal heads, look much like knives found on the northern border of Shang China, a sign that ideas and goods moved along the steppe from end to end.

Where the Karasuk people came from, and what language they spoke, is still argued. They were followed in the Minusinsk Basin by the Tagar culture, part of the wider world of the Scythians.
